samples.summary: New model invariant (MAX_ROW_HEIGHT row-height band) is recorded in no design doc, unlike its listLevel precedent
samples.evidence: This delta adds a new model module `packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts` defining a numeric band for `TableData.rowHeights` and exports it from both package entry points. The directly analogous listLevel band was recorded in prose in `docs/design/docs/docs.md:175-188` ("The *numeric* band is ... an invariant of the model ... `normalizeListLevel()` clamps it at both read boundaries"), and CONTRIBUTING.md:13-14,59-61 requires the design doc to be updated for a non-trivial change and folded into the canonical subsystem doc. Neither canonical table doc is touched: `docs/design/docs/docs-tables.md:80` still describes `rowHeights` as an unbounded optional pixel array, and `docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-resize.md:45-49,204-209,248` still shows the pre-change layout snippet (`const userHeight = tableData.rowHeights[r]`) and a constraint table listing only the 20px floor with no ceiling. A reader of the design docs cannot learn that heights are clamped to 10000 or that a non-finite height reads as auto. (Nested design docs are not link-checked by CI, so nothing else catches this.)

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (plural) is a speculative export with no call site anywhere
samples.evidence: `normalizeRowHeights` is defined and exported but never imported: a repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeight` shows only `normalizeRowHeight` (singular) used in `crdt-tree.ts:203`, `table-layout.ts:253`, `yorkie-doc-store.ts` and the new test; the plural helper appears only at its own definition. It is also not re-exported from `src/index.ts` or `src/node.ts`, so it is dead surface the listLevel precedent (`list-level.ts`, which has no array variant) did not need. Unused API on a hardening module invites future callers to normalize an array once and assume the entries stay clamped.

samples.summary: Paste sanitizer still admits any finite rowHeight; the band is enforced in the view layer instead of at the model boundary that exists for it
samples.evidence: `sanitizeTableData` rebuilds untrusted pasted table data and is the model-level trust boundary — for the analogous field it clamps inline (`clipboard.ts:348-351`, `Math.min(MAX_LIST_LEVEL, Math.max(0, Math.trunc(level)))`). For row heights it still does `table.rowHeights = sourceIndices.map((i) => asNumber(rawHeights[i]))` with no band, and the change instead compensates in the view layer (`table-layout.ts:253`), whose own comment admits "the paste path (`sanitizeTableData`) admits any finite number". The result is a model object that violates the invariant `row-height.ts:11-12` claims ("a number every reader can trust"), which is then persisted back to the CRDT via `Doc.updateTableAttrs`, and a guard placed one layer below the boundary that already owns this validation — inconsistent with the listLevel design the module says it mirrors.

samples.summary: `Doc.setRowHeight` write path does not apply the new band, so the model can still store an out-of-band height
samples.evidence: `document.ts:1180-1184` writes `td.rowHeights[rowIndex] = height` and forwards it to `store.updateTableAttrs` without `normalizeRowHeight`. The new module positions itself as the single definition of the band ("so the band has one definition" is the listLevel wording), and the write side is where a value could be repaired at its source (drag, docx import via `docx-importer.ts:335`, or any future API caller) rather than clamped again in every reader. Behaviour is unaffected today because `computeTableLayout` clamps, but the invariant is enforced only on readers, so the stored/serialized document remains out of band.

samples.evidence: The PR's task plan (issue #1050, "changing a list item's level carries its nested children") scopes the work to `listLevel` planning plus the hardening items listed under "Review follow-ups" (lines 62-77), all of which name `normalizeListLevel` sites.
